transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Solutions Eng), Jamal Ortiz (CTO, Formative), Sara Nguyen (ML Engineer), Liam Patel (DevOps), Emily Ross (Product)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency/throughput) comparing Redwood vs baseline provider (CloudX AI). Discussed tuning levers (batching, quantization, KV/prefix caching), infra differences (A100 vs H100), outlier tail latency, and next steps to run additional tests and share artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:10] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal here, hey.
[00:12] Sara Nguyen: Sara on the ML side.
[00:15] Liam Patel: Liam, infra.
[00:17] Emily Ross: Emily product.
[00:20] Alex Chen: Great, we ran the week-over-week benchmark, we have the spreadsheet link in the chat, alex.redwood.com/benchmarks - please ping me if you don't have it. We'll walk through high level numbers then Priya will go into tuning.
[01:05] Priya Desai: Quick context — baseline provider is CloudX AI for these runs, their stock 8xA100 cluster. For Redwood we ran on H100 reserved pool and on A100 dev nodes to give apples-to-apples. Tests included 512 and 1024 seq lengths, batch sizes 1,4,8, and 2500 request sample for p95/p99.
[02:10] Sara Nguyen: One note, our app more often sees 1-2k token responses not always 512. so curious about longer seqs.
[02:20] Priya Desai: Yep we'll cover 2048 follow-ups as an action.
[03:00] Marco Ruiz: First slide — overall throughput (tokens/sec). Redwood H100 shows ~1.6x throughput vs CloudX A100 at batch 4 for 1024 seq; A100 on Redwood is within 10% of baseline. There are some variance windows we can talk about.
[04:05] Jamal Ortiz: That 1.6x is great but what about tail latency? p99 is what kills UX for us.
[04:20] Priya Desai: p99 on Redwood H100 at batch1 is ~420ms vs CloudX's ~520ms for same model, so better but still some spikes. p95 is tighter ~220ms vs 300ms. We believe spikes are caused by occasional kernel fallback and cache misses.
[05:00] Liam Patel: Can you clarify kernel fallback? we run mixed workloads on our infra, does that affect this?
[05:10] Priya Desai: Sure — sometimes when sequence lengths jump the compiled kernels need to change, and that can introduce latency hiccups. Our runtime does on-the-fly kernel switching but we also have planned js— sorry planned warmup paths and precompiled kernels for typical seq lengths to reduce that.
[06:00] Sara Nguyen: Are you using KV cache / prefix caching for these runs? our production workload benefits a lot there.
[06:10] Marco Ruiz: Yes we ran both cold and warm cache scenarios. With prefix/KV caching enabled p99 drops ~30% for multi-turn reuse cases. We included both sets in the sheet — look at tabs named warm_cache vs cold_cache.
[07:00] Emily Ross: The spreadsheet names are a bit messy, can you send the direct link to the warm cache tab?
[07:08] Alex Chen: Will do after the call.
[07:40] Priya Desai: Now throughput vs batch — for batch 8 we see Redwood A100 and CloudX similar tokens/sec but Redwood H100 gives ~2.1x at batch8 for 512 tokens. So if you care about bulk throughput Redwood H100 has clear advantage.
[08:30] Jamal Ortiz: How about cost delta? we can't just pick speed ignoring unit economics.
[08:40] Priya Desai: Agreed. We ran cost-per-1M tokens with our reserved pricing assumptions. For latency-sensitive config (batch1, low latency), Redwood on H100 is slightly higher per token than CloudX A100, but because of higher throughput at batch sizes that fit your peak bursts, the effective cost per served user is often lower. We included a cost-model tab w/ assumptions.
[09:30] Liam Patel: What about network egress and region differences — our users are EU first and CloudX has eu-west1 capacity. Redwood's private options — will region affect latency?
[09:45] Marco Ruiz: Region only matters for hosted; for Redwood Dedicated/Private you can provision in eu-west. For the hosted tests these were all in us-west, which may add 40-60ms for EU users. For dedicated we can put instances in eu-west and we expect similar numbers to H100 runs here.
[10:30] Sara Nguyen: Any issues around model versions? were the models identical?
[10:40] Priya Desai: We used the same open checkpoint and verified parameter counts; minor tokenization differences caused <1% token count variance across runs. We also matched quantization levels — some runs used fp16, others int8 q4 — noted in the sheet.
[11:20] Jamal Ortiz: int8? our concern is quality regression with quantization. how did you assess output quality?
[11:30] Marco Ruiz: We include a small eval set of 500 prompts and ran A/B comparisons and automated metric checks (perplexity, exact-match, human spot-checks). For q4 int8 we saw <1.5% drop on our eval metrics for your prompt set; we flagged a few corner cases in the notes.
[12:30] Emily Ross: that's useful, can you share the eval prompts and redwood's regression report?
[12:37] Alex Chen: yes, link will be shared post-call, plus the human spot-check comments.
[13:00] Priya Desai: Next — tail behavior: we instrumented kernel-level metrics and found 2 classes of spikes: cold cache + long seq conversion, and GPU contention in mixed tenancy on A100 nodes in baseline provider. On Redwood Dedicated we've seen less contention due to reserved pools.
[14:05] Liam Patel: So contention is the big difference? that sounds like an ops / SLA question.
[14:15] Marco Ruiz: Exactly. For baseline CloudX runs we saw occasional long-tail when noisy neighbors hit GPU IO. With Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity that disappears in our tests.
[15:00] Sara Nguyen: Curious about KV cache invalidation when model updates happen. how durable is it?
[15:10] Priya Desai: KV cache persists per session and is invalidated on model version change; we expose hooks to prewarm caches on rollout to avoid cold-start regressions.
[15:45] Jamal Ortiz: Security — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs for the PII paths. have you provided those docs?
[15:55] Alex Chen: We shared SOC2 and security overview in the security kit, and can provide KMS/HSM integration runbook. We'll add the redwood audit log snippet for your compliance team.
[16:30] Emily Ross: Good, procurement will need those. timing?
[16:35] Alex Chen: We'll push those in the doc share today.
[17:10] Priya Desai: Back to tuning — we recommend three experiments: 1) run 2048 seq length latency sweep (batch1/4) to see tail, 2) test int8 q4 with small eval sets to validate quality regressions, 3) run dedicated-reserved vs hosted burst to see contention effects. We'll run (1) and (2) from our side with access windows you provided.
[18:05] Jamal Ortiz: For the dedicated-reserved test we'll need cost numbers and lead time.
[18:10] Alex Chen: We'll include pricing scenarios for reserved capacity and typical lead times in next update.
[18:40] Marco Ruiz: Quick note — for the 2048 seqs we saw memory pressure on A100 which caused fallback to multi-pass attention in some fibers; H100 handled single-pass more consistently. We'll reproduce and give you the mem/alloc traces.
[19:20] Sara Nguyen: Can you share the traces? that's critical for our infra teams.
[19:25] Priya Desai: Yes we'll attach GPU kernel logs and memory profiles.
[20:00] (short break in conversation while Alex posts links)
[21:10] Alex Chen: Shared: spreadsheet, eval set link, kernel traces placeholder. ping me if access issues.
[22:00] Jamal Ortiz: Looking at the numbers live — curious about the warm_cache p99 for batch4, Redwood looks much better; what's the config?
[22:15] Priya Desai: That's with aggressive prefix caching and our continuous batching disabled for that scenario to avoid batch-induced latency. You can see tradeoff in the batching tab.
[23:30] Liam Patel: Continuous batching disabled? we rely on batching for efficiency at peak— can we have a policy that enables batching only above X QPS?
[23:40] Marco Ruiz: Yes, our runtime supports dynamic batching thresholds and QPS-based policies; we can configure that per-route.
[24:30] Sara Nguyen: Did you test concurrency scenarios with many short requests? our traffic pattern is lots of short chats concurrently.
[24:40] Priya Desai: We did a concurrent short-requests test — Redwood maintained lower p95 under concurrency due to smarter micro-batching and request shaping. CloudX showed p95 degradation when concurrent connections spiked.
[25:10] Jamal Ortiz: Any limitations for on-prem? we may prefer private deployment.
[25:20] Alex Chen: For private we provide a control plane and on-prem compute package; we support KMS integration and offline audits. We'll coordinate with your security team to scope network requirements.
[26:00] Emily Ross: Ok procurement will need the SOW and lead times.
[26:10] Alex Chen: noted, we'll send SOW draft.
[27:00] Priya Desai: Quick note on quantization: in a few corner prompts q4 created tokenization mismatches; we can whitelist those and fall back to fp16 for those prompt templates.
[27:45] Sara Nguyen: Good, fallback policy sounds reasonable.
[28:10] Marco Ruiz: Regarding model rollouts, we support canary at 5/20/100% with automatic rollback if eval metrics degrade. That can be tied to your eval suite.
[29:00] Jamal Ortiz: Nice — can we plug our own eval harness?
[29:10] Priya Desai: Yes, you can provide the harness; we'll run automated checks and trigger alerts on regressions.
[30:00] Emily Ross: Are there any surprises in the raw logs we should know?
[30:10] Priya Desai: One surprise — in CloudX baseline runs there was an unexplained 3% failure rate on long seqs due to RPC timeouts; we couldn't reproduce in Redwood dedicated. We're attaching the failure traces.
[31:00] Liam Patel: We'll want to rerun baseline on our side to confirm reproducibility; I'll carve out a maintenance window.
[31:10] Jamal Ortiz: When's the next sync?
[31:15] Alex Chen: Proposed next sync w/c 2026-04-20 after we run the 2048 tests.
[31:25] Emily Ross: Works for product and procurement check-ins.
[32:00] Priya Desai: For immediate follow-ups, we'll: run 2048 seq tests, run H100 vs A100 throughput batch sweep, and produce a combined cost-latency tradeoff slide.
[32:30] Marco Ruiz: I'll include mem traces and kernel logs in a zipped artifact.
[33:00] Jamal Ortiz: On pricing we'll need a 6-month reserved quote.
[33:10] Alex Chen: We'll include 6/12/24 month scenarios.
[33:45] Sara Nguyen: A couple of nitty-gritty infra asks: can we get perf counters per request and an API to pull p95/p99 by route?
[33:55] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics and you can pull via API. We can enable higher retention for your trial data if needed.
[34:30] Liam Patel: Data residency question — do logs contain PII? we need redaction options.
[34:40] Priya Desai: Logs are configurable and we can enable automatic redaction and partial logging for PII-sensitive workloads; for private deployments you control retention.
[35:10] Emily Ross: ok thanks.
[35:30] (brief cross chatter about calendar invites)
[36:00] Alex Chen: Recap — action items and owners in the chat. We'll share updated spreadsheet, kernel logs, traces, and SOC2 + SSO/KMS docs today. SE will run the 2048 and H100/A100 tests and deliver results by next Wednesday.
[36:45] Jamal Ortiz: That works. Also please include the eval prompts and human spot-check notes.
[36:55] Priya Desai: yes will attach.
[37:30] Marco Ruiz: Any final blockers?
[37:40] Jamal Ortiz: None from me. procurement will evaluate the SOW.
[38:00] Emily Ross: We're good.
[38:10] Alex Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and confirm next meeting time.
[38:20] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR imperfections and occasional speaker label drift; timestamps approximate.
